entities.title: Samosa
entities.summary: The game, its Worker, its address and its database. Also the ruling family that stands in for the Landowners faction (SAMOSAS on screen).
notToBeConfusedWith: Dictator, the 1983 game it remakes, whose name, text and look it does not use.

entities.title: Reign
entities.summary: One game: from the welcome screen, month by month, until the President is killed or escapes, then the rating and the final report.

entities.title: Month
entities.summary: One turn of a reign: the mood roll, accounts, an audience, dangers, a decision, news, a possible revolution and the report offer, in RULES §4's order.

entities.title: Group
entities.summary: One of eight, always in this order: Army, Peasants, Landowners, Guerrillas, the Neighbour, the secret police, the East and the West. Each has a popularity; the first six also have a strength.

entities.title: Faction
entities.summary: One of the three domestic groups that ask favours and may plot: Army, Peasants and Landowners.
notToBeConfusedWith: Group: every faction is a group, not every group is a faction.

entities.title: SAMOSAS, CONTRAS, HONDURAS, SEC. POLICE, EAST, WEST
entities.summary: The labels the screens give the Landowners, the Guerrillas, the Neighbour, the secret police (State Security) and the two superpowers (Moscow and Havana; Washington). The code uses the neutral names.

entities.title: Popularity
entities.summary: How well a group regards the President, 0–9 (POP. on screen).

entities.title: Strength
entities.summary: How powerful one of the first six groups is, 0–9 (STR. on screen).
notToBeConfusedWith: The President's strength, the bodyguard, which has no upper limit.

entities.title: Bodyguard
entities.summary: The President's own strength: 4 at the start, +2 per bodyguard decision with no upper limit, −1 per bankrupt month.

entities.title: Threshold
entities.summary: This month's hidden disaffection line, 2–4. A group whose popularity is at or below it is disaffected.

entities.title: Revolution strength
entities.summary: This month's figure, 10–12, that a faction and its ally's strengths must reach together to plot a revolution. It is shown on every report.

entities.title: Plot
entities.summary: What a disaffected faction plans: a revolution with an ally strong enough, otherwise an assassination. Worked out at every plot check.

entities.title: Ally
entities.summary: The first disaffected group (not the faction itself) whose strength, with the faction's, reaches the revolution strength.

entities.title: Report
entities.summary: State Security's file: every group's popularity and strength, and every plot. The first is free; afterwards it is offered once a month, at the month's end, for $1,000 if the police are loyal and strong and the treasury can pay.

entities.title: Request
entities.summary: The favour a faction asks at the month's audience: one of 24 (R1–R24), eight from each faction, each used once until all 24 have been.

entities.title: Decision
entities.summary: One of 19 presidential options (D1–D19) in five sections of the decision menu; at most one a month.
notToBeConfusedWith: An owner's decision, recorded in a decisions file.

entities.title: Money
entities.summary: Counted in whole thousands of dollars: a treasury of 1000 is $1,000,000.

entities.title: Rating
entities.summary: A reign's score: total popularity of all eight groups, plus 3 a month; if the President got out alive, plus 10 and 1 for every 10 thousand in Switzerland.

entities.title: Best
entities.summary: The best rating so far in this browser, shown on the welcome screen.
notToBeConfusedWith: The high-score table, which is public and kept by the server.

entities.title: Seed
entities.summary: A 32-bit number that fixes every random draw in a reign. The server issues it so that it can replay the reign.

entities.title: Key log
entities.summary: Every key the engine received in a reign, in order, one per screen shown: what the browser sends to be replayed.

entities.title: Held screen
entities.summary: A screen the original moved on by itself. It draws in full and holds for at least its old time reading no key, then shows the any-key footer, and moves on by itself 7 seconds after it appeared unless a key comes first.

entities.title: Footer
entities.summary: The counterfoil in rows 21–23 with the prompt and a flashing cursor: it means the screen is waiting for a key.

entities.title: Baseline
entities.summary: The owner's faithful recreation of the original, in a private repository. Only the spec and verify role reads it; the parity run compares Samosa with it.

entities.title: Games hub
entities.summary: The site's games Worker in another repository: the sign-in pages under /auth/, /games/me and /games/play.js.
